topic.title: We will not be open-sourcing for the second milestone prize

comments.content:
Thanks for letting us know.

I’ll share my solution publicly if I make the top 3 in Milestone 2 among participants who have indicated their willingness to share their solutions.
That's a surprising decision. Hopefully teams can still find large enough improvements to separate themselves from the noise.

Thanks for being transparent about it.

I don't think we will share either. Reason maybe be different as we value medals and ranking way more than money prize. we donate all money prize to charity.

Where I fully agree with you is that the risk of 4000 near identical solutions is very high. We see it in arc agi2 with all public notebooks being tiny variations on our last year solution, and a massive cluster on the leaderboard around these notebooks.

We will open source our code at the end of competition if we end up in gold. As usual for NVIDIA teams.

Would this be an appropriate time to also ask if the host should ask for new model freeze X days before the end of competition because new models cause step-changes in the leaderboard? (Similar to AIMO)

From Game Theory perspective I don't think it is worth it.

The team basically sacrifices $25k for a better chance of gaining $40k. Tufa still has competition-winning talents and resource levels (which then can further re-invests the $25k on if they feel they are in danger of losing the spot).

There is also the risk that other 18-score competitors will also share and take that $25k and bolster their own chance instead. So this only makes sense to do if Tufa is really certain that they have a further secret sauce, but not enough to the point breaking over the potential variance coming from introducing this solution. But that is further the case to just get the $25k.
I don't think they are focused on exact prize money, i think it has more to do with risk of being milestone winner but not competition winner because of the noise introduced by 4000 copies.

Between

  • Skipping Milestone 2 prize, 75% probability of winning 1st place in ARC-AGI-3
  • 100% probability of winning 1st place in Milestone 2 prize, 50% probability of winning 1st place in ARC-AGI-3

Tufa Labs might stronger prefer the first option over the second option even though the expected value is lower (30k vs 25k + 20k).

The achievement of "1st place in ARC-AGI-3" is much more meaningful than "1st place in Milestone 2 prize".
This is a fair point :)). if none of the top 5 shares the solution, then you might be 3rd my friend lol

I also think doing this carries quite a bit of risk, unless none of the current top 5 teams share their solution. Otherwise, Tufa’s concern would still materialize, and they would also miss out on the Milestone 2 prize money.
I agree. There is a case someone might fork the #3 or #4 notebook and become #1
You have a commanding lead. My guess is part of that is some fine tuning, but I just got to #38 on harness fixes alone (5.19) so there's still room for many to climb.
Fair decision given how many teams could copy the solution so close to the deadline. I’m also looking forward to seeing the final solution after the competition ends.
Thanks for the transparency. What are they feeding you guys at Tufa? You guys are cracked!
I think the major advantage is of gpus, they have 10s of TB of gpu vram, allowing continuous testing of different harnesses, and if they need to test new models it wont take much time for them
Just gonna say, congrats to Lord Han Solo, life comes at you fast.
Absolutely fair. The second milestone prize is a bit too far to the deadline I guess!

That is a very interesting take . Really appreciate your solution from the first milestone as well as the transparency in advance . Excited to see what you have been cooking when you finally release your solution .
Absolutely, my original agent scored zero despite 36% on the public set. Without the duck agent, I would never have gotten my start attacking the hidden set. Thank you!
Does the milestone prize move down the ladder or it has to be top 3?

It moves down the ladder, so if the highest scoring open-sourced notebook is actually in 15th place on the leaderboard, but the teams paced 14th - 1st don't open source, then the 15th place open source solution becomes the "1st" place prize winner for the milestone.

Thanks for sharing your intention early!

I also want to ask regarding the rules

Notebooks must be made public under an open source license by the corresponding milestone dates to qualify for these prizes.

Based on precedent (Milestone 1), it seems that

  • Top teams will publish their notebook (together with all the dependencies needed to run the notebook) one or two hours before the deadline
  • Other teams that simply clone and submit the notebook will not be able to get the full score within the one or two hours
  • The ranking priority is based on the snapshot at the deadline (submissions that are in progress will not be considered)
  • If a fine-tuned model is used, the model has to be published before the deadline (because it is part of the dependency to the notebook)

There is something I want to clarify

  • If you fine-tune a model, to be considered for the milestone prize, do you need to publish (1) the dataset and (2) the fine-tuning script?

Congrats on 1st place! Could anyone help clarify this for you?

Also, if I use reasoning traces generated by a proprietary model like Astra to train my public model, would that be okay as well?
